::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Aug 4th 1875  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection C0171: Box 29
:::

My dear [Miss Frere](people/person_525.qmd)

You have chosen a very cold summer for your visit to England and I am afraid you must think you have come there in the winter by mistake. We have had some revolutions in the state of the [Monthly Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd), a new [partner](people/person_373.qmd) at [Mozley](organizations/other_108.qmd)’s[^1] and a new printer, and my effort for some time past has been to get old material finished up. I have still so many verses on hand that I think I had better return yours.

For the story I think there will probably be room for it about July, if you feel able to go on with it. Eleven months hence sounds a long allowance, but one has to live beforehand with magazines<sup>2</sup>

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Although Augusta Frere signed several contributions of fiction to *MP*, and her cousin Emily Frere some non-fiction, the story is not identifiable.
